title: Kestrel and the Wolf
premise: Yara Whitlock has spent a decade as the invisible keeper of the Hollowgate, recording trades in impossible things for a guild that prefers its ledgers clean and its keepers silent. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, Yara learns the gate was never theirs to guard alone: it was sealed by a covenant between realms, broken by the guild itself. Hunted by both sides and bound to a wolf-shaped exile from the other realm named Kestrel, Yara must gather the scattered signatories of the old covenant and reforge it before the unlit dark between worlds devours both. In the end, Yara chooses love over duty—sealing the gate with their own name instead of Kestrel's sacrifice—and steps into a new life neither invisible nor alone.
about_author: Vesper Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about doors, debts, and the people brave enough to knock.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A quiet night at Hollowgate is interrupted by a trade gone wrong—a client sells a memory that shouldn't exist. Yara records it, hides it, and reveals the loneliness beneath their careful invisibility. Emotional beat: the ache of being essential and unseen.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The border wards fail and every star vanishes at once; through the dead gate comes a wounded wolf who speaks with a human voice. The guild's enforcers arrive hunting the intruder, forcing Yara to lie for the first time. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of choosing a side.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Carried
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The wolf, an exiled covenant-keeper named Kestrel, carries half of a shattered seal-stone and memories of a betrayal by the guild's founders. Yara tends their wounds and hears the other realm's version of history. Emotional beat: reluctant trust kindling between strangers.

chapters.title: The Guild of Quiet Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Summoned before the guildmaster, Yara discovers the ledgers themselves were designed to erase the covenant's existence. Refusing to falsify the record, they flee with Kestrel into the borderlands. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity—the first home Yara has ever known becomes a trap.

chapters.title: Signatories
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yara and Kestrel seek the first surviving signatory: a river-goddess turned ferrywoman who remembers the covenant's original promise. She agrees to help only if Yara admits aloud what the gate means to them. Emotional beat: naming what you want before you can fight for it.

chapters.title: The Dark Between
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Crossing the dying borderlands, they witness what the broken covenant unleashes—places unraveling, people forgetting their own names. Kestrel confesses their exile was self-chosen penance for the night the wards first cracked. Emotional beat: guilt confronted, forgiveness offered but not yet accepted.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The second signatory, the guildmaster herself, is found—not a traitor but a hostage of her own founding oath. She reveals the reforge requires a life freely given, and Kestrel has already decided to be that life. Emotional beat: dread as Yara realizes what love against duty truly demands.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Racing the encroaching dark to the last signatory—Yara's own predecessor, alive and hidden inside the gate—they learn the covenant's final clause: any keeper may seal it, if they surrender their name to the ledger forever. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into an impossible choice.

chapters.title: Hollowgate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the gate, with the guild, the goddess, and the gathering dark all converging, Kestrel moves to give their life—but Yara writes their own name into the ledger first, claiming the sacrifice. The covenant reforges around Yara's willing heart. Emotional beat: climax—love answering duty not with obedience but with choice.

chapters.title: Everything That Stays
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The stars return, changed but burning. Yara, nameless in the old ledger but newly named by those who love them, rebuilds Hollowgate not as a prison but a meeting place—with Kestrel staying, no longer exile or sacrifice. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging found not in hiding, but in being chosen.
